prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 2 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 9 of 19 earlier cases, t = 0 in 10; when indemnified t per pc about 79 (80% range 71 to 87); revealed per pc: 38-44 (case 25*), >=68 (case 18), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27) (* = other policy wording)
- line 10 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 9 of 19 earlier cases, t = 0 in 10; when indemnified t per pc about 79 (80% range 71 to 87); revealed per pc: 38-44 (case 25*), >=68 (case 18), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27) (* = other policy wording)

items.rationale: Rainwater entered from outside, so this is flood under 2.5, not escape of water under 2.4. No group (c2) cover is evidenced, so 3.6.2(b) bars the labour; if covered, 12 hours at €90 gross would total €1,080.
Section 3.6.2(f) bars every journey charge for this uninsured flood. The €79 estimate is conditional on coverage and reflects the ordinary charge for the first journey allowed by 7.1.7(g).

Section 3.6.2(d) bars flood-response equipment, and 5.2.2 independently disallows separate pump procurement alongside the extraction charge. The positive figure is a notional gross procurement estimate.
Sections 3.6.2(d) and 5.2.2 bar this separate working-equipment charge; the pump belongs in the price of the extraction measure. The positive figure is a notional gross deployment charge.
Pumping is a mitigation measure under 5.2.2, but 3.6.2(d) bars it when the flood is uninsured, even if the work was urgent. The conditional estimate includes labour and pump use.
Section 3.6.2(c) bars materials installed to repair damage from this uninsured flood. If covered, 7.1.7(c) would limit reimbursement to comparable materials actually used in the rewiring.

items.description: Renew boiler, flue and storage tank
items.rationale: Fixed heating plant is insured property under 4.2.2, but 3.6.2(a) bars replacement after an uninsured flood. The conditional estimate is for a like-for-like installed system under 7.1.1(c), excluding the separately billed pipe adaptation and disposal.
Section 3.6.2(a) expressly bars adaptation work for replacement after an uninsured flood. The conditional estimate covers only the adjoining pipework changes needed to fit the boiler under 7.1.7(d).
Section 3.6.2(e) bars disposal after an uninsured flood, so 5.2.1 does not provide separate cover. The conditional estimate allows for ordinary removal, haulage and disposal.
Section 3.6.2(f) bars the charge; even in a covered event, 7.1.8(d) excludes a second journey charge across trades. The €79 figure is the conditional benchmark for a single allowable journey.
